title: Adaptive kernel negotiation and compile fallbacks for MHA/GQA/MoE with sequence-slice routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add an adaptive negotiation layer to the model-onboarder that picks a primary kernel profile by model architecture (MHA, GQA, MoE) and sequence-length slice, with a graded compile-and-fallback plan. This ticket covers: (1) a negotiation API to request/record preferred kernel profiles per model version and sequence-slice histogram; (2) a compile fallback matrix and runtime routing hints to gracefully switch to compatible kernels when the primary profile is unavailable or fails; (3) telemetry surfaces and gating to drive profile promotion/pinning decisions. Goal is to reduce regression incidents during onboarding and improve tail latency for mixed sequence-length workloads while keeping publish/pin UX simple for model owners.
background: We onboarded several MoE and hybrid-attention models where a single compile profile doesn't perform well across sequence length distributions. Current flow publishes one pinned profile per model version which caused regressions when traffic skewed (longer prefixes) or when optimized kernels failed on certain hardware. Product wants per-model guarantees without multiplying pinned artifacts. This ticket experiments with sequence-slice-aware profile negotiation + graded fallbacks so we can: 1) prefer specialized kernels for common slices, 2) auto-fallback to broader/safer kernels, 3) collect telemetry to promote which slice->kernel pairings should become pinned profiles.
acceptance_criteria: Negotiation API implemented: model-onboarder can record preferred kernel profiles for up to 5 sequence-length slices per model-version
Compile fallback matrix created and stored in profile metadata; runtime honors fallback order when dispatching
Runtime metrics emit slice-level latency, failure-rate, and fallback-rate to /metrics and console dashboards
End-to-end QA: runbench shows no >10% tail latency regression for MoE/GQA models across synthetic traffic mixes compared to baseline
Documentation: onboarding guide updated with negotiation API usage and fallback semantics
tasks: Design negotiation API schema and metadata shape (profile priorities, sequence slices, compatibility tags)
Extend model-onboarder service to accept slice-profile bundles and persist to catalog
Enhance compiler pipeline to emit compatibility tags and fallback candidates for each compiled artifact
Runtime dispatch: integrate negotiation lookup and implement fallback ordering and safety timeouts
Telemetry: add slice labels to existing traces/metrics and create a console dashboard for slice-level SLOs
E2E tests: create synthetic traffic generator for mixed sequence-lengths and validate fallback correctness
Docs & onboarding checklist: update Confluence and quickstart scripts for model owners
notes: Trade-offs considered: storing multiple pinned artifacts increases catalog size and management complexity; we favor a negotiated primary + graded fallback to keep pinned count low while enabling specialization
Compatibility tagging is preferred over hard binary compatibility checks so we can express "stable-on-arch-x" and "slow-but-correct" modifiers for kernels
Fallback ordering should prioritize latency-preserving kernels, then memory-safe kernels, then compatibility-only kernels (in that order)
We will limit slice count to 3-5 to keep lookup costs manageable; slices should be defined by percentiles (p50, p90, p99 cut points) derived from onboarding telemetry
Potential failure mode: oscillation where runtime keeps switching between profiles under borderline metrics; mitigate with hysteresis and cooldown windows

2025-03-01: Runtime dispatch prototype routes to primary profile; added fallback fallback-order config, observed a corner-case where MoE experts had memory blowups when switching; adding safety timeout to cache restore

risks: Increased catalog artifacts if negotiation promotes multiple pinned profiles; need lifecycle policy to garbage-collect stale compilations
Incorrect slice definitions can cause suboptimal routing; require sampled traffic replay to validate slice boundaries
Complex fallback chains may mask underlying compilation bugs; we will gate automatic promotion behind manual QA for the first 3 models
